title: What Is UPI AutoPay? How Recurring UPI Mandates Work
metaDescription: UPI AutoPay lets a merchant debit your bank account on a schedule after one approval. Learn how mandates, limits and pre-debit alerts work, and how to cancel one.
h1: What is UPI AutoPay and how do recurring UPI mandates work?
summary: UPI AutoPay is an NPCI feature that lets you approve a recurring payment mandate once with your UPI PIN, after which the merchant can debit your linked bank account on the agreed schedule. You get a pre-debit notification before each debit, and you can pause or revoke the mandate at any time from the UPI app where you created it.

sections.heading: How UPI AutoPay works
paragraphs: UPI AutoPay was launched by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) in 2020 to bring recurring payments to UPI. When you subscribe to a service, the merchant sends a mandate request to your UPI app. The request shows the merchant name, the amount (fixed or a maximum), the frequency and the validity period.

You approve the mandate once by entering your UPI PIN. After that, the merchant can collect each instalment on schedule without asking you to approve it again, as long as the amount stays within the limits of the mandate and the rules set by the RBI.

sections.heading: Limits and pre-debit notifications
paragraphs: Under RBI rules for recurring e-mandates, debits up to ₹15,000 per transaction can go through without an extra authentication step. For some categories, such as mutual fund subscriptions, insurance premiums and credit card bill payments, the RBI raised this limit to ₹1 lakh. Above the applicable limit, you need to approve each debit with your UPI PIN.

Before each debit you should receive a pre-debit notification, at least 24 hours in advance, telling you the amount and the date. This notification is your window to pause or cancel the mandate if you no longer want the service.
list: Frequencies supported include one-time, daily, weekly, fortnightly, monthly, bi-monthly, quarterly, half-yearly and yearly.
A mandate can be for a fixed amount or for a maximum amount that the merchant debits as needed.
Mandates live in the UPI app where you approved them, under a section usually called AutoPay or Mandates.

sections.heading: Why UPI AutoPay leads to forgotten payments
paragraphs: The convenience that makes AutoPay useful also makes it easy to forget. A free trial turns into a paid plan, an annual renewal arrives a year after you stopped using the service, or a mandate sits in a UPI app you rarely open. Because nothing asks you to act, small recurring debits can add up to thousands of rupees a year.
Cancelling the subscription inside the service and revoking the UPI mandate are two separate steps. Doing only one of them can leave the other active, so it is worth checking both.

sections.heading: How to keep track of your mandates
paragraphs: Review the AutoPay section of every UPI app you use at least once a quarter. Note down each active mandate, its amount, frequency and next debit date, then revoke the ones you no longer need.

A manual-first tracker such as Essara makes this easier: you add each mandate and subscription once, Essara converts it into a monthly and yearly cost, and the renewal dates stay visible in one place across Android and the web — without connecting your bank account.

faqs.a: UPI AutoPay mandates need your UPI PIN to be created, you receive a pre-debit notification before each debit, and you can pause or revoke a mandate at any time from your UPI app. As with any payment method, only approve mandates from merchants you trust.

faqs.q: What is the UPI AutoPay limit without a PIN?
faqs.a: Recurring debits up to ₹15,000 per transaction can be processed without extra authentication. For mutual fund subscriptions, insurance premiums and credit card bill payments the limit is ₹1 lakh. Debits above the applicable limit need your UPI PIN each time.

faqs.q: Does cancelling a subscription also cancel the UPI AutoPay mandate?
faqs.a: Not always. Some merchants revoke the mandate when you cancel, but many do not. Check the AutoPay or Mandates section of your UPI app after cancelling and revoke the mandate there if it is still active.

faqs.q: Where can I see all my UPI AutoPay mandates?
faqs.a: Each UPI app shows only the mandates created in it, usually under a section called AutoPay, Mandates or Manage payments. If you use several UPI apps, check each one, or keep a single list in a tracker such as Essara.
